title: Gapped text: The Great Emu War

passages.title: The Great Emu War
passages.intro: 5 sentences have been removed. Choose the sentence that best fits each gap. There is one extra sentence you do not need.
passages.credit: Original text written for this practice.
paragraphs: In 1932, farmers in Western Australia faced an unusual enemy. About 20,000 emus had moved into the wheat-growing district around Campion, trampling crops and breaking fences. [[1]]
The government agreed to help, and sent a small group of soldiers armed with machine guns. [[2]] The emus, however, had other ideas.

Whenever the soldiers approached, the birds scattered in every direction, running at up to 50 kilometres an hour. [[3]] Even when the soldiers mounted a gun on a truck, the bumpy ground made it impossible to aim.
After about a week, the soldiers were withdrawn. [[4]] Newspapers around the world reported on the 'war', and many joked that the emus had won.
Today, farmers use stronger fences rather than soldiers to keep emus away from crops. [[5]] Historians still use the story as a reminder that nature does not always behave the way people expect.

bank.A: Although they returned briefly later in the year, the campaign never achieved what was hoped.
bank.B: Emus lay large, dark green eggs.
bank.C: Their plan was simple: find the flocks and shoot as many birds as possible.
bank.D: This made them extremely difficult targets.
bank.E: The farmers, many of them former soldiers, asked the government to send help.
bank.F: The emu, meanwhile, appears on the Australian coat of arms.
